newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API crude drop seen mainly Hurricane quirk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API crude drop seen mainly Hurricane quirk.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 07/25/97 WEEK ENDED 07/25/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 1.75 MLN 119,305 DN 0.835 MLN
GASOLINE........ DN 1.70 MLN 194,631 DN 3.172 MLN
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.50 PCT PT 96.1 DN 0.60 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
A much larger than expected drop in U.S. crude oil inventories last week is a quirk that was largely due to the effect of Hurricane Danny, analysts said Tuesday.

The huge 9.7 million-barrel drop in nationwide crude stocks reported Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute (API) didn't gel with other data showing refinery runs down, gasoline production off and crude oil imports generally steady, the analysts said.
"I think the crude numbers will easily be dismissed. They will probably be overwhelmed by the product numbers," said Tom Knight, a petroleum products trader at Fina.
"The only thing you can really say is that (refinery) runs are fairly steady," said Paulo Nery, an industry analyst at Pace Consultants in Houston.

Nevertheless, September crude oil futures rose sharply and were up 25 cents at $20.10 a barrel in after-hours trading on the New York Mercantile Exchange's ACCESS system just before 1800 EDT/2200 GMT.

The API report showed the big drop in crude stocks while at the same time showing crude runs down nationwide at 14.7 million barrels per day (bpd) from 14.9 million bpd the previous week, and crude oil imports down only marginally at 8.138 million bpd from 8.145 million bpd.

"Adding to the Hurricane situation, Canadian imports were down and that may be another factor but I still cannot see that big a decline in one week. Runs are down and overall imports are hardly changed," said Nizam Sharif, an analyst at Hornsby & Co. consultants in Houston.
Indeed, Canadian crude imports dropped some 30 percent in the week ended July 25, from 1.024 million bpd to 723,000 bpd, according to the API report.
But the biggest drop in crude stocks came in the PADD III district (the U.S. Gulf region) which contains the largest concentration of U.S. refiners as well as most of the nation's crude production.

Hurricane Danny ripped through the Gulf and landed in southern Louisiana and Mississippi last week, causing some offshore fields to shut-in production temporarily, as well as a slow-down or shut-down for some refineries, including Chevron Corp's 295,000 bpd plant in Pascagoula, Mississippi.

The short-term closure or slow-down in plant might explain the decline in actual crude runs in the East of the Rockies regions, even while operating capacity rose to 101.1 percent from 100.2 percent, said Nery.

Meanwhile, "implied demand" for gasoline, which is arrived at by looking at production, imports and stocks, showed a decline to 8.6 million bpd last week from 8.8 million bpd, with a drop of more than three million barrels in stocks offset by lower imports.

"Implied demand may level off at the 8.4/8.6 (million bpd) level for the next couple of weeks and if production gets back to normal levels we should see a nominal decline for the next few weeks as imports come in," Sharif said.
August gasoline futures were up 1.63 cents at 66.47 cents a gallon in regular trading Tuesday and a further 0.83 cents at 67.30 in ACCESS just before 1800 EDT.

"The gasoline numbers pretty much confirmed what the cash market has been doing for the last week," said Knight of Fina, referring to the sharp gains seen on both the U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor due to a tight market.
"Also, we had strong distillate demand and no builds in inventories, which I think may surprise a lot of people," Knight added.
--Tony McAuley, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1623
